Executable example PASS:

- Access Control ALLOW proof verifies;
- session Security Manager permits the exact protected method only through PermissionAuthority;

Security properties exercised:

- cryptographic attribution does not imply Access Control authority;
- attributed principal must equal the request principal at both Access Control and Permission authorities;
- Access Control is a separate coarse domain-entry decision;
- contextual Access Control attributes are deterministic and fail closed on missing/mismatched values;
- Access Control request attributes are snapshotted against post-seal caller mutation;
- protected-domain composition requires a cryptographically proved Access Control ALLOW by default;
- successful building/domain entry does not grant any protected method permission;
- Permission remains exact subject × object × method and requires Security Effect evidence bound to the same exact object and method;
- a second object of the same class is denied when only the first object identity is granted;
- Security Manager blocks denied protected methods before their body executes;
- Access Control and Permission decisions retain verifiable Crypto key-ring MAC proofs;
- both policy types publish and resolve through Institutional Policy v0.8;
- default DENY and deterministic DENY-wins-equal-priority semantics remain tested.
